lesson.menu_title: Laís Presents — A Real Class Presentation in English
lesson.menu_desc: Standing up, twelve minutes, in front of everybody -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Laís Presents: A Real Class Presentation in English
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Laís Paludetto Rodrigues | Lesson 9 -- Laís Presents

listenings.text: A few things before you start planning. First, do not try to memorise the whole thing. Students who memorise stop breathing after two minutes and then they panic. Learn your outline instead, and let the sentences happen. Second, I want you to practise standing up, out loud, at home. Reading it silently is not rehearsing, it is reading. Third, and this is the one everybody ignores: decide how you are going to finish before you decide how you are going to start. People remember the last twenty seconds. And if you run out of time, do not speed up. Skip a slide and keep your ending. Nobody has ever complained about a presentation that finished early.

Hey, it's Sam. So mine was today and it did not go how I expected, so I'm telling you before yours. I spent about four hours making the slides look nice and about fifteen minutes practising the actual talking, and you can guess which of those two things mattered. I forgot to look up. I read the screen for eleven minutes and I have no idea if anybody was listening. Also I planned to finish with the good part, and then I ran out of time and I skipped it, which is the one thing you should never skip. If I did it again I'd practise standing up in my room, out loud, with the door closed, and I'd stop caring about the font.

extra_audio.text: Lais writes the outline before she opens the slides. She decides how the presentation is going to finish and works backwards from there. She rehearses standing up, out loud, three times in her room. On the day she looks up at the audience instead of reading the screen. She finishes twenty seconds early and takes two questions.

items.situation: Open a presentation about your exchange without saying "hello my name is and today I am going to talk about".
tips: Six months ago I had never seen snow.
I want to start with one photograph.
This is the street where I grew up.

items.situation: You forget a word in the middle of a sentence, in front of the class. Recover out loud, without stopping.
tips: Sorry, how do I say this...
The word I want is escaping me.

items.situation: Move from one part of the presentation to the next, out loud.
tips: That's the school. Now the food.
The second thing I want to point out is...

items.situation: You are two minutes over and the teacher is looking at the clock. Land the ending anyway.
tips: And that's why I chose this photograph.

items.situation: Somebody asks a question you do not know the answer to. Answer honestly and keep your credibility.
tips: That's a good question and I don't know.

items.situation: Finish. Say the last twenty seconds, which are the ones people remember.
tips: If you remember one thing, remember this.
Thank you. I'm happy to answer questions.
